questions.q: What does disabling a user account via Microsoft Graph in this lesson's playbook actually do?
options: Deletes the user object permanently from Microsoft Entra ID
Sets accountEnabled to false, blocking new sign-ins and revoking existing sessions on next token refresh
Sends the user a password reset email with no other effect
Only flags the account for a future manual review, with no immediate effect
questions.explain: The PATCH call sets accountEnabled to false on the account, which blocks new sign-ins and revokes existing sessions once tokens refresh -- an immediate, real change of state.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say disabling the wrong account or isolating the wrong device is a different category of mistake than a bad enrichment lookup?
options: It costs more in Azure consumption charges to run
Enrichment mistakes are impossible, so there's nothing to compare
Both mistakes are equally harmless since they can be undone instantly
A wrong containment action has high blast radius -- locking out a real employee or isolating a domain controller -- unlike a bad enrichment lookup, which fails safely
questions.explain: Enrichment failing just means someone reads an extra, unnecessary line of context. A wrong containment action changes real-world state and can cause the exact outage or disruption it was meant to prevent.

questions.q: In the Logic App pattern this lesson builds, what structurally prevents the Disable_user_account action from running without human involvement?
options: A comment is posted to the incident reminding the analyst to check the action manually afterward
The playbook only runs during business hours
The action is wrapped in a Condition that only evaluates true when the approval card's response equals "approve" -- there is no path to it otherwise
Azure automatically rate-limits any account-disable call to once per day
questions.explain: The workflow literally cannot reach the destructive action unless the If condition on the approval response evaluates true, and that only happens because a specific person clicked Approve.

questions.q: What should happen in the playbook when an approval request is rejected?
options: The playbook retries the same approval request immediately without logging anything
Nothing -- a rejection requires no record since no action was taken
The containment action runs anyway after a short delay
A comment is still written to the incident recording that containment was declined, by whom, and why
questions.explain: A rejected approval should still produce a comment, so the incident record shows a human looked and chose not to act -- not that the playbook silently did nothing.

questions.q: What does Microsoft Defender for Endpoint's device isolation do, as described in this lesson?
options: Cuts the machine off from the network while leaving Defender's own management channel intact, so investigation can continue
Physically powers down the device remotely
Permanently removes the device from Microsoft Entra ID
Only disables the device's local administrator account
questions.explain: Isolation cuts off general network access while preserving Defender's management channel, so the device can still be investigated and managed without being able to spread further.
